title: Localization of a module at one element, and the canonical maps M_f -> M_{fg}
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module and $f\in R$. The *localization of $M$ at $f$* is the $R_f$-module $M_f=S^{-1}M$ for $S=\{1,f,f^2,\dots\}$: its elements are the classes $m/f^e$ ($m\in M$, $e\ge0$) of pairs $(m,f^e)$, where $m/f^e=m'/f^{e'}$ if and only if $f^k(f^{e'}m-f^em')=0$ for some $k\ge0$, with $m/f^e+m'/f^{e'}=(f^{e'}m+f^em')/f^{e+e'}$ and $(x/f^d)(m/f^e)=xm/f^{d+e}$; together with the $R$-linear *localization map* $M\to M_f$, $m\mapsto m/1$. In particular $m/1=0$ iff $f^km=0$ for some $k$, and $f$ acts bijectively on $M_f$. For $g\in R$, $f$ acts bijectively on $M_{fg}$, so by the universal property of $M\to M_f$ (an $R$-linear map from $M$ to a module on which $f$ acts bijectively factors uniquely through $M_f$) there is a unique $R$-linear map $M_f\to M_{fg}$ with $m/1\mapsto m/1$; it is $m/f^e\mapsto g^em/(fg)^e$, the *canonical map*. (For $M=R$ this is the ring $R_f$ of [def-weil-ring-localization-away].)
